title: Product labelling using the metric system is introduced
text: A system of measurement is a frame in which physical qualities can be quantified with numbers. Among many systems of measurement, the metric system refers to ones that standardise a set of base units and a nomenclature describing relatively large and small quantities using decimal-based multiplicative unit prefixes (such as kilo and milli).

title: John Damien, a racing steward at Woodbine Racetrack, is fired from his job for being gay, sparking a legal battle that eventually leads to the inclusion of sexual orientation in the Ontario Human Rights Code in 1986.
text: Woodbine Racetrack is a race track for Thoroughbred horse racing in the Etobicoke area of Toronto, Ontario, Canada. Owned by Woodbine Entertainment Group, Woodbine Racetrack manages and hosts Canada's most famous race, the King's Plate.

title: Sylvia Ostry is appointed Canada's first female Deputy Minister.
text: Sylvia Ostry was a Canadian economist and public servant.

title: Television cameras are allowed to film in Parliament
text: Television is a telecommunication medium for transmitting moving images and sound. Additionally, the term can refer to a physical television set rather than the medium of transmission.

title: The beaver becomes an official symbol of Canada
text: The North American beaver is one of two extant beaver species, along with the Eurasian beaver (Castor fiber). It is native to North America and has been introduced in South America (Patagonia) and Europe (primarily Finland and Karelia).

title: Alberta election: Peter Lougheed's PCs win a second consecutive majority
text: Edgar Peter Lougheed was a Canadian lawyer and Progressive Conservative politician who served as the tenth premier of Alberta from 1971 to 1985, presiding over a period of reform and economic growth. Born in Calgary, Alberta, Peter was the son of Edgar Donald Lougheed and Edna Alexandria Bauld and grandson of Canadian Senator Sir James Alexander Lougheed, a prominent Alberta businessman.

title: Environment Canada switches to degrees Celsius
text: Environment and Climate Change Canada is the department of the Government of Canada responsible for coordinating environmental policies and programs, as well as preserving and enhancing the natural environment and renewable resources. It is also colloquially known by its former name, Environment Canada (EC; French: Environnement Canada).

title: The CN Tower is completed in Toronto
text: The CN Tower is a 553.3-metre-high (1,815.3 ft) communications and observation tower in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. Completed in 1976, it is located in downtown Toronto, built on the former Railway Lands.

title: Brampton Centennial Secondary School shooting
text: On May 28, 1975, a school shooting occurred at Brampton Centennial Secondary School in Brampton, Ontario, Canada. The perpetrator, 16-year-old Michael Slobodian, a student at the school, shot and killed two people and injured 13 others before committing suicide.

title: The Yukon and the Northwest Territories are given seats in the Senate
text: The Senate of Canada is the upper house of the Parliament of Canada. Together with the Crown and the House of Commons, they compose the bicameral legislature of Canada.

title: Saskatchewan election: Allan Blakeney's NDP win a second consecutive majority
text: Allan Emrys Blakeney was a Canadian politician who served as the tenth premier of Saskatchewan from 1971 to 1982. Originally from Bridgewater, Nova Scotia, Blakeney moved to Regina, Saskatchewan, and worked in the province's civil service before running for office with the Co-operative Commonwealth Federation (CCF) under Tommy Douglas.

title: Prime Minister Pierre Trudeau announces the creation of the Foreign Investment Review Agency
text: Joseph Philippe Pierre Yves Elliott Trudeau was a Canadian politician, lawyer, jurist, academic, author, and journalist who served as the 15th prime minister of Canada from 1968 to 1979 and from 1980 to 1984. He served as the leader of the Opposition from 1979 to 1980.

title: David Lewis is replaced by Ed Broadbent as leader of the NDP
text: David Lewis was a Canadian labour lawyer and social democratic politician. He was national secretary of the Co-operative Commonwealth Federation (CCF) from 1936 to 1950 and one of the key architects of the New Democratic Party (NDP) in 1961.

title: Petro-Canada, the government-owned oil and gas company, is formed.
text: Petro-Canada is a retail and wholesale marketing brand subsidiary of Suncor Energy. Until 1991, it was a federal Crown corporation.

title: CKND, Winnipeg's newest television station, begins broadcasting
text: CKND-DT is a television station in Winnipeg, Manitoba, Canada, owned and operated by the Global Television Network, a division of Corus Entertainment. The station's studios are located on the 30th floor of 201 Portage in downtown Winnipeg, with transmitter atop the building.

title: John Turner resigns from government to protest the implementation of wage and price controls.
text: John Napier Wyndham Turner was the 17th prime minister of Canada, serving from June to September 1984. He served as leader of the Liberal Party and leader of the Opposition from 1984 to 1990.

title: Ontario election: Bill Davis's PCs win a minority
text: William Grenville Davis was a Canadian politician who served as the 18th premier of Ontario from 1971 to 1985. Behind Oliver Mowat, Davis was the second-longest serving premier of Ontario.

title: Mirabel Airport opens
text: Montréal–Mirabel International Airport, originally called Montréal International Airport, widely known as Mirabel and branded as YMX International Aerocity of Mirabel, is a cargo and former international passenger airport in Mirabel, Quebec, Canada, 21 nautical miles (39 km; 24 mi) northwest of Montreal. It opened on October 4, 1975, and the last commercial passenger flight took off on October 31, 2004.

title: St. Pius X High School shooting: Robert Poulin kills one person and wounds five at St. Pius X High School in Ottawa, before shooting himself.
text: On 27 October 1975, a mass shooting took place at St. Pius X High School in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada.
wiki: St. Pius X High School shooting

title: CBC-FM rebranded as CBC Stereo
text: CBC Music is a non-commercial Canadian FM radio network operated by the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation. It began by primarily concentrating on classical and jazz music.

title: The SS Edmund Fitzgerald, based in Sault Ste. Marie sinks
text: SS Edmund Fitzgerald was an American Great Lakes freighter that sank in Lake Superior during a storm on November 10, 1975, with the loss of the entire crew of 29 men. When launched on June 7, 1958, she was the largest ship on North America's Great Lakes and remains the largest to have sunk there.

title: Canada's first community-based campus radio station, CKCU-FM in Ottawa, hits the airwaves
text: Campus radio is a type of radio station that is run by the students of a college, university or other educational institution. Programming may be exclusively created or produced by students, or may include program contributions from the local community in which the radio station is based.

title: Canadair nationalized
text: Canadair Ltd. was a Canadian civil and military aircraft manufacturer that operated from 1944 to 1986.

title: William R. Bennett sworn in as Premier of British Columbia, replacing David Barrett.
text: William Richards Bennett, was a Canadian politician who was the 27th premier of British Columbia from 1975 to 1986.

title: Izzy Asper acquires Winnipeg television station CKND, the beginning of what would become a national media empire.
text: Israel Harold "Izzy" Asper was a Canadian tax lawyer and media magnate. He was the founder and owner of the now-defunct TV and media company Canwest and father to its former CEO and President Leonard Asper, former director and corporate secretary Gail Asper, and former Executive Vice President David Asper.

title: Rohinton Mistry emigrates to Canada
text: Rohinton Mistry is an Indian-born Canadian writer. He has been the recipient of the Neustadt International Prize for Literature in 2012.

title: First Canadian Place opens in Toronto
text: First Canadian Place is a commercial skyscraper in the Financial District of Toronto, Ontario, at the northwest corner of King and Bay streets, and serves as the global operational executive office of the Bank of Montreal. At 298 metres tall, it is the third-tallest building in Canada, the 35th-tallest building in North America, and the 261st-tallest in the world.

title: Colin Thatcher, who would later become famous for his involvement in the murder of his ex-wife, is elected to the Saskatchewan Legislative Assembly.
text: Wilbert Colin Thatcher is a Canadian politician who was convicted for the murder of his ex-wife, JoAnn Wilson.

title: In June, 1975 Ovivo, a water and wastewater treatment and purification company, is founded in Quebec as Laperrière & Verreault Inc. (rebranded in 2010).
text: Ovivo is a water and wastewater treatment and purification company. The company is owned by SKion Water GmbH, a subsidiary of German entrepreneur Susanne Klatten’s investment holding SKion GmbH. Ovivo's Head Office is located in Montreal, in the province of Quebec.

title: Alberta Golden Bears won their Third University Cup by defeating the Toronto Varsity Blues 2 games to 1. All the games were played at Northlands Coliseum in Edmonton
text: Northlands Coliseum is a defunct indoor arena in Edmonton, Alberta. It was used for sports events and concerts, and was home to the Edmonton Oilers of the World Hockey Association and National Hockey League (NHL), and the Edmonton Oil Kings of the Western Hockey League (WHL).

title: Toronto Marlboros won their Seventh (and Final) Memorial Cup by defeating the New Westminster Bruins 7–3. The Final game was played at the Kitchener Memorial Auditorium Complex
text: The Memorial Cup is the national championship of the Canadian Hockey League (CHL), a consortium of three major junior ice hockey leagues operating in Canada and parts of the United States. It is a four-team round-robin tournament played among the champions of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL), Quebec Maritimes Junior Hockey League (QMJHL) and Western Hockey League (WHL), and a host team, which alternates on an annua…

title: Houston Aeros won their Second (and Final) Avco Cup by defeating the Quebec Nordiques 4 games to 0. The deciding game was played at the Colisée de Québec
text: The Avco World Trophy, also known as the Avco Cup, is the playoff championship trophy of the defunct World Hockey Association, which operated from 1972 until 1979. The trophy's naming rights were sold to the former Avco Corporation, a defense contractor who bought the rights to advertise their consumer finance division.

title: Montreal, Quebec's Bernie Parent of the Philadelphia Flyers is awarded his Second Conn Smythe Trophy
text: Bernard Marcel Parent was a Canadian professional ice hockey goaltender who played 13 National Hockey League (NHL) seasons with the Philadelphia Flyers, Boston Bruins, and Toronto Maple Leafs between 1965 and 1979, and also spent one season in the World Hockey Association (WHA) with the Philadelphia Blazers during the 1972–73 season. Parent is widely acknowledged as one of the greatest goaltenders of all time.

title: Ottawa Gee-Gees won their First Vanier Cup by defeating the Calgary Dinos by a score of 14–9 in the 11th Vanier Cup played at Exhibition Stadium in Toronto
text: The Vanier Cup is the trophy awarded annually to the champion Canadian football team in U Sports, the governing body for university sports in Canada. The U Sports football champion is determined in a one-game playoff (the Vanier Cup game), played by the winners of the Uteck Bowl and the Mitchell Bowl.

title: Edmonton Eskimos won their Fourth Grey Cup by defeating the Montreal Alouettes 9 to 8 in the 63rd Grey Cup played at McMahon Stadium in Calgary
text: The Grey Cup is both the championship game of the Canadian Football League (CFL) and the trophy awarded to the victorious team playing in the namesake championship of professional Canadian football. The game is contested between the winners of the CFL's East and West divisional playoffs and is one of Canadian television's largest annual sporting events.

title: World of Wonders - Robertson Davies
text: William Robertson Davies was a Canadian novelist, playwright, critic, journalist, and professor. He was one of Canada's best known and most popular authors and one of its most distinguished "men of letters", a term Davies gladly accepted for himself.

title: A Fine and Private Place - Morley Callaghan
text: Edward Morley Callaghan was a Canadian novelist, short story writer, playwright, and TV and radio personality.

title: The Unwavering Eye: Selected Poems, 1969-1975 - Irving Layton
text: Irving Peter Layton, OC was a Romanian-born Canadian poet. He was known for his "tell it like it is" style which won him a wide following but also made him enemies.

title: It's Me Again - Donald Jack
text: Donald Lamont Jack was an English and Canadian novelist and playwright.

title: The Island Means Minago - Milton Acorn
text: Milton James Rhode Acorn, nicknamed The People's Poet by his peers, was a Canadian poet, writer, and playwright.

title: Jacob Two-Two Meets the Hooded Fang - Mordecai Richler
text: Mordecai Richler was a Canadian writer from Montreal, Quebec. He is best known for his novels set in Montreal's Jewish community; including The Apprenticeship of Duddy Kravitz (1959) and Barney's Version (1997).

title: Un jardin au bout du monde - Gabrielle Roy
text: Gabrielle Roy was a Canadian author from St. Boniface, Manitoba.

title: Jardin des délices - Roch Carrier
text: Roch Carrier is a Canadian novelist and short story author. He is among the best known Quebec writers in English Canada.

title: See 1975 Governor General's Awards for a complete list of winners and finalists for those awards.
text: Each winner of the 1975 Governor General's Awards for Literary Merit was selected by a panel of judges administered by the Canada Council for the Arts. The council established four annual Canada Council Children's Literature Prizes in 1975, two each for children's book writers and illustrators, which remained outside the "Governor General's Awards" rubric through 1986.

title: Stephen Leacock Award: Morley Torgov, A Good Place to Come From
text: The Stephen Leacock Memorial Medal for Humour, also known as the Stephen Leacock Medal for Humour or just the Leacock Medal, is an annual Canadian literary award presented for the best book of humour written in English by a Canadian writer, published or self-published in the previous year. The silver medal, designed by sculptor Emanuel Hahn, is a tribute to well-known Canadian humorist Stephen Leacock and is accom…
wiki: Stephen Leacock Memorial Medal for Humour

title: Vicky Metcalf Award: Lyn Harrington
text: The Vicky Metcalf Award for Literature for Young People, colloquially called the Vicky, is given annually at the Writers' Trust Awards to a writer or illustrator whose body of work has been "inspirational to Canadian youth". It is a top honour for Canadian children's writers and Canadian children's book illustrators.
wiki: Vicky Metcalf Award for Literature for Young People

title: Anne Murray and Oscar Peterson each win a Grammy Award.
text: Oscar Emmanuel Peterson was a Canadian jazz pianist and composer. As a virtuoso who is considered to be one of the greatest jazz pianists of all time, Peterson released more than 200 recordings, won eight Grammy Awards, as well as a lifetime achievement award from the Recording Academy, and received numerous other awards and honours.

title: Paul Anka - Times of Your Life is released
text: Paul Albert Anka is a Canadian and American singer-songwriter and actor. His songs include "Diana", "You Are My Destiny", "Lonely Boy", "Put Your Head on My Shoulder" and "(You're) Having My Baby".

title: Joni Mitchell - The Hissing of Summer Lawns
text: Roberta Joan Mitchell is a Canadian and American singer-songwriter, multi-instrumentalist, and painter. As one of the most influential singer-songwriters to emerge from the 1960s folk music circuit, Mitchell became known for her personal lyrics and unconventional compositions, which grew to incorporate elements of pop, jazz, rock, and other genres.

title: Saturday Night Live, produced by Canadian Lorne Michaels and also featuring Paul Shaffer and Dan Aykroyd, premieres in the United States.
text: Lorne Michaels is a Canadian and American television and film producer, screenwriter and director. He created and produced Saturday Night Live (1975–1980, since 1985) and produced the Late Night series (since 1993), The Kids in the Hall (from 1988 to 1995), and The Tonight Show (since 2014).

title: “Kung Fu Fighting” by Carl Douglas
text: "Kung Fu Fighting" is a disco song by the Jamaican-British vocalist Carl Douglas, written by Douglas and produced by British-Indian musician Biddu. It was released in 1974 as the first single from his debut album, Kung Fu Fighting and Other Great Love Songs, on the cusp of a chopsocky film craze and rose to the top of the British, Australian, Canadian, and American charts, in addition to reaching the top of the So…

title: “Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds” by Elton John
text: "Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds" is a song by the English rock band the Beatles from their 1967 album Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band.
wiki: Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds
listen: Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds Elton John

title: “Please Mr. Postman” by The Carpenters
text: "Please Mr. Postman" is a song written by Georgia Dobbins, William Garrett, Freddie Gorman, Brian Holland and Robert Bateman.

title: “Doctor's Orders” by Carol Douglas
text: "Doctor's Orders" is a song written by Roger Cook, Roger Greenaway and Geoff Stephens which, in 1974, was a hit in the United Kingdom for Sunny of Sue and Sunny; in the United States the song was a hit for Carol Douglas.

title: “Mandy” by Barry Manilow
text: "Brandy", later called "Mandy", is a song written by Scott English and Richard Kerr. It was originally recorded by English in 1971 and reached the top 20 of the UK Singles Chart.

title: “Best of My Love” by Eagles
text: "Best of My Love" is a song written by Don Henley, Glenn Frey, and JD Souther. It was originally recorded by the Eagles, and included on their 1974 album On the Border.

title: “Have You Never Been Mellow” by Olivia Newton-John
text: "Have You Never Been Mellow" is a song recorded by British-Australian singer Olivia Newton-John for her 1975 fifth studio album of the same name. Written and produced by John Farrar, the song was released as the lead single from the album in January 1975.
listen: Have You Never Been Mellow Olivia Newton-John

title: “Lady Marmalade” by Labelle
text: "Lady Marmalade" is a song written by Bob Crewe and Kenny Nolan and popularized in 1974 by the American funk rock group Labelle. It is best known for its French refrain of "Voulez-vous coucher avec moi, ce soir?", a sexual proposition that translates into English as "Do you want to come to bed with me, tonight?" Released as a single on November 5, 1974, Labelle's version held the number-one spot on the Billboard H…

title: “No No Song” by Ringo Starr
text: "No No Song" is a 1974 song by English musician Ringo Starr. Written by Hoyt Axton and David Jackson, it appeared on Starr's 1974 album, Goodnight Vienna.

title: “Philadelphia Freedom” by Elton John
text: "Philadelphia Freedom" is a song by British musician Elton John and lyricist Bernie Taupin, and performed by John. It was released as a single on 28 February 1975, credited to the Elton John Band.

title: “I Don't Like to Sleep Alone” by Paul Anka
text: "I Don't Like to Sleep Alone" is a song written by Paul Anka and performed by Anka featuring Odia Coates. It was featured on his 1975 album Feelings.
wiki: I Don't Like to Sleep Alone
listen: I Don't Like to Sleep Alone Paul Anka

title: “It's a Miracle” by Barry Manilow
text: "It's a Miracle" is a 1975 single by Barry Manilow and was the second release from his album, Barry Manilow II. "It's a Miracle" went to number twelve on the U.S. Billboard Hot 100 and was Manilow's second number one on the U.S. Easy Listening chart, spending one week at number one in April 1975. The single also peaked at number fifteen on the disco/dance chart, and was the first of four entries on the chart.

title: “Thank God I'm a Country Boy” by John Denver
text: "Thank God I'm a Country Boy" is a song written by John Sommers and recorded by American singer/songwriter John Denver. The song was originally included on Denver's 1974 album Back Home Again.
wiki: Thank God I'm a Country Boy
listen: Thank God I'm a Country Boy John Denver

title: “Hey You” by Bachman–Turner Overdrive
text: "Hey You" is a song written by Randy Bachman and first recorded by Canadian rock group Bachman–Turner Overdrive for their 1975 album Four Wheel Drive. It was the first and more successful of two singles issued from the LP, the second being "Quick Change Artist", which was released in Canada only.

title: “Love Will Keep Us Together” by Captain & Tennille
text: "Love Will Keep Us Together" is a song written by Neil Sedaka and Howard Greenfield. It was first recorded by Sedaka in 1973.
listen: Love Will Keep Us Together Captain & Tennille

title: “Wildfire” by Michael Murphey
text: "Wildfire" is a song written by Michael Murphey and Larry Cansler. It was originally recorded by Murphey, who had yet to add his middle name to his recorded work, and appears on his gold-plus 1975 album Blue Sky – Night Thunder.

title: “Only Women Bleed” by Alice Cooper
text: "Only Women Bleed" is a song by American rock singer Alice Cooper, released on his debut solo studio album Welcome to My Nightmare. It was written by Cooper and Dick Wagner and was the second single from the album to be released.

title: “Listen to What the Man Said” by Wings
text: "Listen to What the Man Said" is a hit single from Wings' 1975 album Venus and Mars. The song featured new member Joe English on drums, with guest musicians Dave Mason on guitar and Tom Scott on soprano saxophone.
wiki: Listen to What the Man Said
listen: Listen to What the Man Said Wings

title: “Magic” by Pilot
text: "Magic" is a 1974 song by Scottish pop rock band Pilot and was the first hit single for the group. It was written by band members David Paton and Billy Lyall for their debut album From the Album of the Same Name.

title: “The Hustle” by Van McCoy
text: "The Hustle" is a disco song by songwriter-arranger Van McCoy and the Soul City Symphony. It went to No.

title: “Please Mr. Please” by Olivia Newton-John
text: "Please Mr. Please" is a song written by Bruce Welch and John Rostill, both members of British pop singer Cliff Richard's backing band, The Shadows.

title: “Jive Talkin'” by Bee Gees
text: "Jive Talkin'" is a song by the Bee Gees, released as a single in May 1975 by RSO Records. This was the lead single from the album Main Course.

title: “I'm Not in Love” by 10cc
text: "I'm Not in Love" is a song by the English band 10cc, written by band members Eric Stewart and Graham Gouldman. It is known for its innovative and distinctive backing track, composed mostly of multitracked vocals.

title: “How Sweet It Is (To Be Loved by You)” by James Taylor
text: "How Sweet It Is" is a song by the American soul singer Marvin Gaye. Motown issued the song as a single on its Tamla label in November 1964, and in January 1965 it appeared as the title track of Gaye's fifth studio album.
wiki: How Sweet It Is (to Be Loved by You)
listen: How Sweet It Is (To Be Loved by You) James Taylor

title: “Rhinestone Cowboy” by Glen Campbell
text: "Rhinestone Cowboy" is a song written and recorded by Larry Weiss in 1974, then popularized the next year by American country music singer Glen Campbell, and considered to be Campbell's signature song. When released on May 26, 1975, as the lead single and title track from his album Rhinestone Cowboy, it enjoyed huge popularity with both country and pop audiences.

title: “Get Down Tonight” by KC and the Sunshine Band
text: "Get Down Tonight" is a song by American disco and funk band KC and the Sunshine Band, released in February 1975 by TK Records as the first single from their second and self-titled album. The song became widely successful, becoming the first of their five No.
listen: Get Down Tonight KC and the Sunshine Band

title: “The Ballroom Blitz” by Sweet
text: "The Ballroom Blitz" is a song by British glam rock band The Sweet, written by Nicky Chinn and Mike Chapman. The song reached number one in Canada, number two in the UK Singles Chart and the Australian Chart, and number five on the US Billboard Hot 100.

title: “Third Rate Romance” by The Amazing Rhythm Aces
text: "Third Rate Romance" is a song written by Russell Smith, first recorded in Montreal in 1974 by Jesse Winchester and his band the Rhythm Aces, assisted by Smith. It became a hit the following year by the newly re-formed Amazing Rhythm Aces on its 1975 album Stacked Deck.
listen: Third Rate Romance The Amazing Rhythm Aces

title: “I'm Sorry” by John Denver
text: "I'm Sorry" is a song written and recorded by American country-folk singer-songwriter John Denver and released in 1975. It was the final number-one pop hit released during his career.

title: “Black Superman (Muhammad Ali)” by Johnny Wakelin
text: "Black Superman" is a song by English songwriter Johnny Wakelin from his album of the same name. The song reached #7 on the UK Singles Chart and #21 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1975.

title: “Before the Next Teardrop Falls” by Freddy Fender
text: "Before the Next Teardrop Falls" is an American country song written by Vivian Keith and Ben Peters, and most famously recorded by Freddy Fender. His version was a major crossover success in 1975, reaching number 1 on the Billboard pop and country charts.
listen: Before the Next Teardrop Falls Freddy Fender

title: “My Eyes Adored You” by Frankie Valli
text: "My Eyes Adored You" is a 1974 song written by Bob Crewe and Kenny Nolan. It was originally recorded by The Four Seasons in early 1974.
listen: My Eyes Adored You Frankie Valli

title: “Some Kind of Wonderful” by Grand Funk Railroad
text: " Some Kind of Wonderful" is a song written by Canadian-American musician John Ellison and first recorded by his R&B group, Soul Brothers Six, in 1967, peaking at number 91 on the US Billboard Hot 100. The line "She's some kind of wonderful" previously appeared in the song "Too Busy Thinking About My Baby" which was first recorded by The Temptations (released in 1966).
wiki: Some Kind of Wonderful (Soul Brothers Six song)
listen: Some Kind of Wonderful Grand Funk Railroad

title: “Shining Star” by Earth, Wind & Fire
text: "Shining Star" is a song by Earth, Wind & Fire from the album That's the Way of the World, issued as a single in January 1975 on Columbia Records. The song rose to No.

title: “Fame” by David Bowie
text: "Fame" is a song by the English singer-songwriter David Bowie. It was released on his ninth studio album Young Americans and was later issued as the album's second single by RCA Records in June 1975.

title: “Laughter in the Rain” by Neil Sedaka
text: "Laughter in the Rain" is a song composed and recorded by Neil Sedaka, with lyrics by Phil Cody. It includes a 20-second saxophone solo by Jim Horn.
listen: Laughter in the Rain Neil Sedaka

title: “One of These Nights” by Eagles
text: "One of These Nights" is a song by the American rock band Eagles, written by Don Henley and Glenn Frey. The title track from their 1975 One of These Nights album, the song became their second single to top the Billboard Hot 100 chart after "Best of My Love" and also helped propel the album to number one.

title: “Lovin' You” by Minnie Riperton
text: "Lovin' You" is a song recorded by American singer-songwriter Minnie Riperton from her second studio album, Perfect Angel. It was written by Riperton and her husband, Richard Rudolph, produced by Rudolph and Stevie Wonder, and released as the album's third single on November 29, 1974 by Epic Records.

title: “Black Water” by The Doobie Brothers
text: "Black Water" is a song recorded by the American music group the Doobie Brothers from their 1974 album What Were Once Vices Are Now Habits. The track features its composer Patrick Simmons on lead vocals and, in mid-March 1975, became the first of the Doobie Brothers' two No.

title: “(Hey Won't You Play) Another Somebody Done Somebody Wrong Song” by B.J. Thomas
text: " Another Somebody Done Somebody Wrong Song" is an American country song made famous by B. J. Thomas. It won the 1976 Grammy for Best Country Song, awarded to its songwriters Larry Butler and Chips Moman.
wiki: (Hey Won't You Play) Another Somebody Done Somebody Wrong Song
listen: (Hey Won't You Play) Another Somebody Done Somebody Wrong Song B.J. Thomas

title: “He Don't Love You (Like I Love You)” by Tony Orlando and Dawn
text: "He Will Break Your Heart", is a song originally performed and co-written by Jerry Butler. It was a top-ten hit in 1960.
listen: He Don't Love You (Like I Love You) Tony Orlando and Dawn

title: “At Seventeen” by Janis Ian
text: "At Seventeen" is a song by American singer-songwriter Janis Ian from her seventh studio album Between the Lines. Columbia released it in July 1975 as the album's second single.

title: “Pick Up the Pieces” by Average White Band
text: "Pick Up the Pieces" is a song by the Average White Band from their second album, AWB. On the single, songwriting credit was given to founding member and saxophonist Roger Ball and guitarist Hamish Stuart individually and the entire band collectively. It is essentially an instrumental, apart from the song's title being shouted at several points in the song.
wiki: Pick Up the Pieces (Average White Band song)
listen: Pick Up the Pieces Average White Band

title: “Why Can't We Be Friends?” by War
text: "Why Can't We Be Friends?" is a song by American funk band War, from their 1975 studio album Why Can't We Be Friends?. It has a simple structure, with the phrase "Why can't we be friends?" being sung four times after each two-line verse.
listen: Why Can't We Be Friends? War

title: “Love Won't Let Me Wait” by Major Harris
text: "Love Won't Let Me Wait" is a hit 1975 single by Major Harris, a former member of R&B/soul group The Delfonics. Written by Vinnie Barrett and Bobby Eli, the single is considered to be a staple of classic soul playlists, and was Harris' only entry into the top five on both the soul and pop charts.
listen: Love Won't Let Me Wait Major Harris

title: “Boogie On Reggae Woman” by Stevie Wonder
text: "Boogie On Reggae Woman" is a 1974 funk song by American Motown artist Stevie Wonder, released as the second single from his seventeenth studio album, Fulfillingness' First Finale, issued that same year. Despite the song's title, its style is firmly funk/R&B and neither boogie nor reggae.
listen: Boogie On Reggae Woman Stevie Wonder

title: “Wasted Days and Wasted Nights” by Freddy Fender
text: "Wasted Days and Wasted Nights" is an American country and pop song recorded by Freddy Fender. It is considered by many to belong to the swamp pop idiom of south Louisiana and southeast Texas that had such a major musical impact on Fender.
listen: Wasted Days and Wasted Nights Freddy Fender

title: “Angie Baby” by Helen Reddy
text: "Angie Baby" is a song written by American singer-songwriter Alan O'Day which became a hit for Australian singer Helen Reddy. The song reached #1 on the U.S. Billboard Hot 100 chart December 28, 1974, and became one of Reddy's biggest-selling singles.

title: “Fight the Power” by The Isley Brothers
text: "Fight the Power"") is a song recorded by the Isley Brothers; the band released the song as the first single off their landmark album, The Heat Is On. The song is notable for the usage of the word "bullshit", which was censored during radio airplay.
listen: Fight the Power The Isley Brothers

title: “Jackie Blue” by Ozark Mountain Daredevils
text: "Jackie Blue" is a track recorded by the Ozark Mountain Daredevils for their second album It'll Shine When It Shines released in 1974. It was written by band members Larry Lee and Steve Cash with lead vocals by Lee.

title: Science Magazine
text: Science is the peer-reviewed academic journal of the American Association for the Advancement of Science and one of the world's top academic journals. It was first published in 1880, is currently circulated weekly and has a subscriber base of around 130,000.

title: The Bobby Vinton Show
text: The Bobby Vinton Show is a Canadian musical variety television series produced for the CTV Television Network between 1975 and 1978, with a total of 52 episodes broadcast. Featuring Bobby Vinton, a best-selling popular music singer since the early 1960s, the series mixed comedy skits with musical interludes.

title: Grand Old Country
text: Grand Old Country is a Canadian television variety series airing on CTV from 1975 to 1981. The show was hosted by country music singer Ronnie Prophet.

title: Sidestreet
text: Sidestreet is a Canadian television drama, which aired Sundays on CBC from 1975 to 1978. It stars Sean McCann and Donnelly Rhodes as police working in Toronto.

title: The Fifth Estate
text: The Fifth Estate is an English-language Canadian investigative documentary series that airs on the national CBC Television network. The name is a reference to the term "Fourth Estate", and was chosen to highlight the program's determination to go beyond everyday news into original journalism.

title: King of Kensington
text: King of Kensington is a Canadian television sitcom that aired on CBC Television from 1975 to 1980.

title: The Watson Report
text: The Watson Report is a Canadian current affairs television series, seen nationally on CBC from 1975 to 1981. The titular host was Patrick Watson, previously of This Hour Has Seven Days whose interviews for the show included national political leaders.
